records.name: Philly Girls Who Walk
records.summary: A free group for women in Philadelphia that organizes walks, a book club and other social events so members can get moving and meet people.
records.what_you_do: Join a walk or social event with other women in the city. Events are posted on the group's Heylo page, where you sign up.

schedule.text: Walks, a book club and other social events are posted on the group's Heylo page, with a date on each event.

first_step.how: Open the group's Heylo page, pick a walk or social event from the upcoming list, and sign up there.
first_step.basis: The site's Join us button leads to the sign-up page and events are open to women in the city, but the site does not describe how newcomers are welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are walks, a book club and social outings, each with its own card on the Heylo page. The group's aim, as its site presents it, is helping women move more and meet others. Joining is free.
first_visit_tips: Read the event card for the date and any meeting details before you sign up.
Pick a walk that matches your pace from the upcoming list.

records.notes: Heylo lists five upcoming October events by weekday and day of month only, with no year, so they are not used as dated evidence and status stays probably_active. Event times are not recorded because the reader could not confirm them. The /reachout page is for brand partnerships, not members. Heylo is the only way in: the site has no FAQ or volunteer page.

records.name: Philly Improv Theater (PHIT)
records.summary: An improv and acting school in Old City with beginner classes, a longer course, and a monthly Community Night that mixes a short improv show with an open jam.
records.what_you_do: Take a beginner class, such as Intro to Improv or Improv Essentials, or come to Community Night and join the open jam.

schedule.text: Community Night is a monthly show followed by an open jam, held on a Saturday evening at 254 on South 12th Street. Beginner classes run as short courses, from a 90 minute Intro to Improv workshop to a 3 week Improv Essentials clinic.

cost.text: Class prices are not listed on the site. Community Night has a $10 venue cover that goes to the venue, not the group (listed for the October event).

access.notes: The class page says the classroom spaces are accessible and climate controlled.

first_step.how: Register for a beginner class such as Improv Essentials through the class registration page, or come to a Community Night, where no improv experience is needed.
first_step.basis: The site offers beginner clinics and a 90 minute beginner workshop, and says no improv experience is needed to join the Community Night open jam.
first_step.what_to_expect: Community Night is a low pressure evening: a short set of performances by students, alumni and local improvisers, then a host runs the open jam. You can watch, join the jam or just hang out. Classes are short courses that need registration first, and the site does not list class prices.
first_visit_tips: Check the ticket or reservation page before you go, since the site lists an advance reservation link as coming soon.
The October 2026 Community Night was 21 and older with valid ID, so check the age rule for each night.
For the October event, check-in and seating started at 6:15 pm.

records.notes: Community Night is held at 254 (254 S. 12th Street). Another post gives the venue as 215; that is not recorded. The October 17, 2026 event is a Queer Community Night, and its advance reservation link is listed as coming soon. Dated class start dates and an ensemble information session are left out of the schedule. Class prices and class times are not listed on the site.

records.name: Philly Knits
records.summary: A free fiber arts group for knitters, crocheters, weavers and sewers at every skill level. Members meet at various places around the city and online, and the group posts volunteer requests from local charities.
records.what_you_do: Join a meetup, take on a volunteer request from a local charity, or start a meetup in your own neighborhood.

schedule.text: Meets at various places in Philadelphia and online, with no fixed weekly time on the group's site. The site points people to its Meetup page to find upcoming meetups.

locations.label: Various locations in Philadelphia, and online

first_step.how: Email Lynn Landes to ask about the next meetup, or join one from the Meetup page the group links to.
first_step.basis: The site says all skill levels are welcome, offers self-paced beginner lessons, and explains how to join.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group's site does not describe a typical meetup, so check the Meetup page for the next date and place. Meetups cover knitting, crocheting, weaving and sewing, and all skill levels are welcome.
first_visit_tips: For the beginner Learn to Knit lessons, the site lists starter supplies: two balls of yarn, two size 8 needles about 9 inches long, a tapestry needle and small scissors.

records.notes: The group's own pages never mention a Sit and Stitch, so that line from tier 1 was removed. The homepage says the group is looking for a new Meetup organizer (no date given). The Learn to Knit lessons are self-paced, not a scheduled class. The Meetup page is a third-party platform and was not used for facts. Groups.htm names other Philadelphia knitting groups, listed in leads_only.

records.name: Philly LIFTS
records.summary: A City of Philadelphia program that connects families affected by substance use, including families of babies born with withdrawal symptoms, to support groups, recovery help, doula referrals and overdose prevention training.
records.what_you_do: Families get referrals for food, baby supplies, clothing, housing and job help, plus support groups and recovery services. Community giveaways and celebrations are open to all families, not only people enrolled.

schedule.text: Community events are listed on the program's events calendar. The city's online overdose reversal training runs monthly at noon, with registration through a Zoom link.

cost.text: The program pages do not say whether services cost money.

first_step.how: Fill out the Philly LIFTS interest form linked from the services page, or call Carla Calabrese at (215) 776-4406 about the new mothers' support group.
first_step.basis: A public city program with named staff and an interest form for families, though the pages do not describe what a first meeting is like.
first_step.what_to_expect: Your first step is a form or a phone call with program staff, who connect families to referrals and support groups. The new mothers' support group is described as a safe, non-judgmental space.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the overdose prevention training is open to all families. The pages read today give no audience for the training, so that line was removed; only community giveaways and celebrations are stated as open to all families. Therapy and general questions go to Suzannah McNamara (suzannah.mcnamara@phila.gov). Families affected by substance use can also reach Family Care Navigator Roxana Lizarraga (Roxana.LizarragaNavarro@Phila.gov, (267) 624-9577). Status is active on the events calendar, which lists events dated October 2026. The calendar also lists provider meetings, which are not for families.

records.name: North Philly Peace Park
records.summary: A neighborhood-run ecology campus in North and West Philadelphia with free urban farming, education and wellness programs. It also runs a weekly market for local sellers of natural products.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free monthly Self-Care Saturday, shop the weekly market, or bring a school group for a planting or composting visit.

schedule.text: Self-Care Saturdays are monthly and free, with programs such as yoga, fitness, art therapy and cooking. The weekly Black Market features local sellers of natural products, and school visits are arranged in advance.

first_step.how: Come to a free monthly Self-Care Saturday, or email phillypeacepark@gmail.com to ask about the next volunteer day.
first_step.basis: Free public programs at an open site, with an email address to ask questions, though the site does not say it welcomes newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Self-Care Saturdays are free and held monthly, with activities such as yoga, fitness, art therapy and cooking. The campus is a set of gardens, so expect plants and outdoor space. The weekly market features local sellers of items such as soap and candles, many made from garden harvests.

records.notes: The events page lists only undated or old items: a groundbreaking ceremony that is still to come (its timeline says spring 2021) and a First Service Day with no date. Volunteers can write to volunteeratthepeacepark@gmail.com for that day. No item dated 2025 or 2026 was found, so status stays probably_active as a working site. The homepage header gives 2216 W. Jefferson St and 930 N. 51st St; the record keeps 2200 W. Jefferson St, as the site's location list does. Green Wall Street runs the weekly market (see leads_only).

records.name: Philly Pumptrack
records.summary: A bike pump track on Parkside Avenue in West Fairmount Park, where riders practice on a looping course. Volunteers keep the track in shape at dig nights, most Wednesday nights in season.
records.what_you_do: Ride when the track is open, after signing the waiver on arrival (a parent or guardian signs for riders under 18). Volunteers can join dig nights, where gloves and tools are provided.

schedule.text: Open for the season, usually May to late October, weather permitting. Dig nights are most Wednesday nights in season, followed by a barbecue. Ladies-Only and 5 and Under sessions run from 10 am to noon before the track opens, with dates posted on the group's social media. Pumpjam, the season kickoff, is usually the first Saturday in May.

locations.label: Parkside Avenue, next to the Parkside Evans playground, West Fairmount Park

cost.text: No entry fee is shown on the group's site.

first_step.how: Visit during open hours or on a dig night and sign the waiver on arrival. Under 18s need a parent or guardian to sign, and the form can be downloaded ahead of time.
first_step.basis: The site says newcomers can simply show up to dig nights, where gloves and tools are provided, and riders sign a waiver at the track.
first_step.what_to_expect: Dig nights are a work session on the track followed by a barbecue, and the group says new and old volunteers are both welcome. For riding, you sign the waiver on arrival and ride while the track is open.
first_visit_tips: Download the waiver ahead of time or sign it on arrival.
Under 18s need a parent or guardian to sign.
Dig nights provide gloves and tools, so you do not need your own.

records.notes: Status set to dormant under the dated-evidence rule. The newest dated item on the group's own pages is August 2024 (Dig to Ride days on the homepage). The events page gives the start of Dig Night as April 6, 2022, and its other events have no year. The news page is a newsletter sign-up with no dates. A search for 2025 or 2026 items found nothing. The site says the track is open for the season, and its footer shows 2026, but neither is dated evidence. Tier 1 had active with a 2026-10 date from the city friends registry, which I could not reproduce on the group's pages. Please confirm with the group before publishing the dormant label. Hours and camp prices come from 2024 Instagram posts, which are leads-only, so they are not recorded. The address and zip come from the batch record (city friends registry), not from the group's site. Name taken from the site's footer.

records.name: Philly Reading Coaches
records.summary: A City of Philadelphia early reading program. Volunteers sit one on one with a student in grades K to 3 during after school sessions at city out of school time programs.
records.what_you_do: Coaches read with one student for at least one hour a week. No teaching experience is needed, and the city trains volunteers.

schedule.text: Coaches meet one student for at least one hour a week, after school at city out of school time programs.

first_step.how: Fill out the interest form linked from the city's program page, or email PRC@phila.gov.
first_step.basis: The city's program article says no prior experience is required and volunteers get trained, and it explains how to apply.
first_step.what_to_expect: Before your first session you complete an orientation and a mandated reporter training module. You also complete the clearances the program lists, including state and child abuse history checks, an FBI waiver or fingerprint check, and a sex offender registry check for adults.
first_visit_tips: Volunteers aged 16 and 17 need a parent or guardian to sign a release form.
You can read more about the program on the city's page before you apply.
